title: Hom objects into a simplicial semi-representable object turn pushouts of finite simplicial sets into fibre products
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $K$ a simplicial object of the category $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ of semi-representable objects over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. Call a simplicial set $S$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] *admissible* if $S_m$ is finite and nonempty for every $m\geq0$ and $S$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. For admissible $S$ write $H(S)=\operatorname{Hom}(S,K)_0$ with its universal family $(u^S_s)$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object], and for a morphism $f:S\to S'$ of admissible simplicial sets let $f^*:H(S')\to H(S)$ be the unique morphism with $u^S_s\circ f^*=u^{S'}_{f(s)}$ for all simplices $s$ of $S$ (for an inclusion of a simplicial subset this is the restriction morphism). Let $p:A\to B$, $q:A\to C$ be morphisms of simplicial sets and let $D$ with $i:B\to D$, $j:C\to D$ be a pushout of $p$ and $q$ in simplicial sets, with $B$, $C$, $D$ admissible. (a) If $A$ is admissible, then $H(D)$ with $i^*$ and $j^*$ is a fibre product of $p^*:H(B)\to H(A)$ and $q^*:H(C)\to H(A)$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$. (b) If $A$ is empty, then $H(D)$ with $i^*$ and $j^*$ is a product of $H(B)$ and $H(C)$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$.

proof.text: For a test object W, identify an S-family in K over W with a natural transformation from S to the simplicial set n |-> Mor(W,K_n). Use ULift on both sides to put simplex and morphism types in the same universe. The compatibility equations are exactly naturality. The explicit maps familyToNatTrans and natTransToFamily implement this identification, and familyToNatTrans is injective. Whiskering with uliftFunctor preserves colimits by Mathlib's whiskeringRight_preservesColimitsOfShape and ULift colimit-preservation instances. Apply IsPushout.desc to the lifted simplicial pushout to glue agreeing B- and C-families; its two factorization equations give the required restrictions. Apply IsPushout.hom_ext to show that two D-families with the same two restrictions agree. These are the proved private helpers glueFamilies and family_pushout_ext.

The representing property for A makes equality of morphisms to HA equivalent to equality of all universal-family components. Compose iStar followed by pStar and jStar followed by qStar with each component of uA. The equations hp, hq, hi and hj identify the results with uD at the images under p followed by i and q followed by j. The pushout square commutes, so these images agree. Thus iStar followed by pStar equals jStar followed by qStar.

Given a:W->HB and b:W->HC with a followed by pStar equal to b followed by qStar, the B-family a followed by uB and the C-family b followed by uC agree on A, by hp and hq. Glue them by step 1 to a D-family f. Surjectivity of the representing bijection for D supplies l:W->HD carrying uD to f. Injectivity of the representing bijections for B and C proves that l followed by iStar is a and l followed by jStar is b. If two such l have the same projections, step 1 identifies their D-families; injectivity of the representing bijection for D then identifies the morphisms. IsPullback.mk' packages commutativity, existence and uniqueness into the claimed pullback. No independently constructed fibre product, finite-limit existence theorem, or comparison isomorphism is needed.

When every degree of A is empty, any B-family and C-family agree on A by empty elimination. Apply the same gluing and representing-bijection argument to obtain a lift for every pair a:W->HB and b:W->HC, with uniqueness by family_pushout_ext and injectivity for D. BinaryFan.isLimitMk packages these lifts and their uniqueness as the product universal property of HD with projections iStar and jStar. This uses no representing pair for A and no terminal-object or finite-limit construction.

split_report.summary: Split the item directly from Stacks Lemma 017N in degree 0. The proof constructs the fibre product in SR(X), identifies D-families with compatible B- and C-families by the pushout universal property in simplicial sets, transports this bijection through the representing universal properties of H(-), and concludes by the fibre-product universal property. The empty-base case is the same argument with a vacuous compatibility condition and the final object, yielding a product. No additional node was needed because all non-elementary categorical structure is supplied by the existing Hom-object, representing-object, simplicial-set, semi-representable, and finite-limits nodes.
split_report.blueprint: The steps realize the fourth paragraph of lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-refinement's proof ('Previously chosen faces prescribe compatible boundaries'): compatible families on the two pieces of a simplicial pushout are exactly a family on the pushout, and the Hom object therefore is the fibre product.
